I have farmed here in Quzhou County a long time, so I will not start from zero. I will do close to what has paid for me before, then adjust a little for cost and yield. I have 35 mu total, and with well irrigation I will keep 30 mu in the wheat-maize rotation and leave 5 mu for cotton. On wheat land, I will feed it a bit heavier because wheat here responds well when water is available, and I do not want to lose ears for the sake of saving a little fertilizer. On summer maize after wheat, I will still put real fertilizer in, but I will use the wheat stubble and soil moisture, so I will keep tillage lighter and push for a stable grain yield. Cotton is only a small block for me, so I will manage it more carefully by mu because labor and spraying cost more there; cotton needs more watching for insects and a steadier potassium supply, otherwise the bolls and fiber suffer. Since I run 35 mu with only 2 people in the house, I will keep the field work simple, use machinery where it saves labor, irrigate enough times to protect yield, and spend the money first on seed, fertilizer, water, and the key sprays.
